research_question: Does a club's contemporaneous domestic scoring, concession and schedule history improve its first exact score and ordered top three in AFC Champions League Elite, UEFA Champions League, Europa League and Conference League? Fit separately for each competition. All other configured competitions retain their previous assessments.
evidence: Use ESPN numeric team IDs verified against the home and away participants of the specific continental event. Domestic observations must be finished top-flight league fixtures with verified regulation scores. Keep exact raw sources, dates, identity coverage and conflicts. Never infer a club link from a similar name. Earlier domestic data starts 2023-01-01. All fixtures remain in each evaluation denominator, including clubs with no domestic coverage.
features: For each club take up to its last eight domestic games in the preceding 120 UTC days. Exclude every fixture on the date of the target and later. For each domestic game compare its goals for and against with the prior venue-specific home/away scoring means of that domestic league, shrunk with 40 home/away games at 1.4 goals. Use four pseudo-games at 1.4 to shrink each club's observed/expected log ratio. Restrict each log ratio to [-1,1]. Rest pressure uses (5 - min(5, days since last domestic game))/4 and domestic match count in the preceding 14 days divided by four, capped at one. Missing side history has neutral features. These are domestic-schedule proxies; cup, international, and training workloads are not fully observed.
model: For each continental competition independently, fit one shared ridge Poisson log-rate offset model for the two sides against the chronological R7 anchor. Use own domestic attack, opponent domestic concessions, own-minus-opponent short-rest pressure and own-minus-opponent fixture count. Ridge penalty 16, bound coefficients to [-1,1], cap each side's log-rate adjustment to +/-0.55. Exponentially tilt the full R7 matrix by the two fitted log-rate adjustments times home and away goals, preserving the dependence structure of the control. Include the fixed full-dose ablation.
selection: Use only the chronological validation period to choose doses 0, 0.5 or 1 per competition. Use R10's existing rule for its three heads: first exact hits, then three-score hits, then exact-score log loss for the score head; direction hits and full wins on actual Asian lines for the other heads; smallest dose for ties. At zero dose, retain all original control choices. Show exposure on neither, either or both sides.
windows: UEFA uses the original R7 main fits, training before 2024-07-01, validation 2024/25, main test 2025/26 and separate recent 2026/27 test. Separately score any strictly verified UEFA matches completed on 2026-11-24 UTC in the R7 first-issue population, using the first issued price and archived R7 comparator. AFC Elite uses R10's refreshed 2024/25 fit, 2025/26 validation and 2026/27 test, reporting previously known and post-October-12 matches separately. The latter overlaps R10. No model choice uses these test windows.
reporting: Report all four project rates per competition, original R7 and R10 where recorded, a paired chronological R7 control, market coverage, real-line settlement outcomes, first corrections/losses, top-three corrections/losses and paired date-cluster uncertainty. Refit only the predeclared coefficients on completed competition history for prospective inference, retaining validation-selected doses. For a new future research freeze, use intact earlier frozen population identity and markets, cap domestic results at the actual research issue cutoff, preserve every first issue and all previously displayed recommendations. This experiment does not change the active models or the four stage thresholds.
